tell me about the legal ai companion: The Legal AI Companion is an AI-powered personal legal assistant focused on Indian law. It uses a complete RAG pipeline with Document Loading, Text Chunking, Embedding Generation, ChromaDB vector store, Retriever, and local LLMs via Ollama (Llama 3.1) to provide accurate, context-grounded legal guidance.
legal ai architecture: The Legal AI Companion architecture: Document Loading ➔ Text Splitting & Chunking ➔ Embedding Generation (all-MiniLM-L6-v2 / BGE / BERT) ➔ ChromaDB Vector Store ➔ Retriever ➔ LangChain RAG Pipeline ➔ Local LLM (Ollama Llama 3.1) ➔ Final Grounded Response.
legal ai technologies: Python, LangChain, RAG, ChromaDB, BERT, Sentence Transformers, Ollama, Llama 3.1, and Firebase.
legal ai embedding models: all-MiniLM-L6-v2, BGE, and BERT-based sentence embeddings.
why use chromadb: ChromaDB is a high-performance open-source vector database that stores and retrieves high-dimensional document embeddings with fast semantic search similarity.
why use embeddings: Embeddings convert text into dense numerical vectors capturing semantic meaning so similar legal concepts can be retrieved even with different phrasing.
why use a retriever: A retriever queries the vector database using vector similarity search to fetch the most relevant context chunks for the user's prompt.
how does langchain fit into the pipeline: LangChain orchestrates the entire RAG workflow by connecting document loaders, text splitters, vector stores, prompt templates, and the LLM into a unified chain.
how to explain legal ai project to recru: I engineered The Legal AI Companion, an AI assistant for Indian law. I built an end-to-end RAG pipeline using LangChain, ChromaDB vector database, sentence embeddings, and local Ollama Llama 3.1, delivering accurate, context-grounded legal assistance with zero paid API dependency.

what is an epoch: An epoch is one complete cycle through the entire training dataset during machine learning or neural network model training.
what is forward propagation: Forward propagation is the process where input data passes through the neural network layers, calculating activations and loss to produce an output prediction.
what is backpropagation: Backpropagation calculates the gradients of the loss function with respect to weights using the chain rule, updating weights to reduce error.
what is gradient descent: Gradient descent is an optimization algorithm that iteratively adjusts neural network weights in the direction of steepest descent of the loss function.
overfitting and underfitting: Overfitting happens when a model memorizes training noise and fails on new data (high variance). Underfitting happens when a model is too simple to learn underlying patterns (high bias).
bias and variance: Bias is the error from overly simplistic assumptions. Variance is the error from sensitivity to small fluctuations in training data. The goal is the optimal Bias-Variance tradeoff.
what is cnn: A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is a specialized deep learning architecture designed for visual data processing using convolutional layers, pooling, and feature extraction.
what are transformers: Transformers are deep learning architectures based on self-attention mechanisms, allowing parallel processing of text sequences for powerful language models like BERT and GPT.
rag vs fine tuning: RAG retrieves external factual knowledge at query time without retraining, while Fine-Tuning updates the model's internal weights to adapt its style or specific task behavior.
bert vs llama: BERT is an encoder-only model designed for understanding, classification, and embeddings. Llama is an autoregressive decoder model designed for generative reasoning and conversational text generation.
embeddings vs tokens: Tokens are discrete text segments (words or subwords), while embeddings are continuous high-dimensional vector representations capturing semantic meaning.
ai agent vs normal chatbot: A normal chatbot generates single responses based on prompts, while an AI Agent can reason, make decisions, plan multi-step tasks, use external tools, and execute workflows autonomously.
